tasks.prompt: A student reports dizziness during a planned endurance activity. Explain the immediate response, an appropriate reporting step, and how the learning objective can still be assessed.
Create an inclusive 5-day introductory movement plan that combines warm-up, comfortable aerobic activity, strength technique, mobility, recovery and two alternative participation pathways.

Two fictional learners show different practice logs. One has fewer minutes but specific technique reflections; the other records only duration. Explain what each log supports and what additional evidence is needed.
Develop a sustainable four-week activity plan with activity choices, safety cues, rest, adaptations, low-cost alternatives and observable process goals.
Critique the statement 'the fastest and strongest students learned the most.' Explain why this is not a valid PE mastery criterion and propose an equitable evidence-based rubric.

A student has limited access to equipment and a changing schedule. Compare two safe movement options, justify an accessible plan and explain how to monitor progress without collecting sensitive health data.

Select three dated examples of your learning across the year, identify one corrected misconception and defend one improvement to your future activity plan. A written, spoken, observed or adapted demonstration is acceptable.

teacherContract.notes: This file is an instructional assessment specification, not a grading service. Local journal submissions remain drafts until independently reviewed.
